params.body:
## Why

`dealers.carpass_password` held every dealer's Car-Pass password in plain text, and the settings tab
rendered it straight back into the input (`value="{{$dealer->carpass_password}}"`). So the login of
every garage at Car-Pass was readable in any dump, any backup and any read on that table, and it also
travelled to every browser that opened the tab and back on every save. Car-Pass is a paid, per-lookup
service tied to the dealer's identity, so that credential is worth stealing.

This is the same shape as PR 258 did for `warranty_password`, one layer lower: there the value was
already encrypted and only the echo was wrong; here the column itself was in the clear.

## What

- **Model.** `App\Models\Settings\Dealer` gets `protected $casts = ['carpass_password' => 'encrypted']`.
  Every reader is unchanged: `CarpassController::withDealerAuth($dealer->carpass_username,
  $dealer->carpass_password)`, `CarpassSmoke`, `IntegrationSmoke` all keep reading the attribute and
  keep getting the plain value. What is on disk is ciphertext bound to `APP_KEY`.
- **Migration** `2026_09_13_000100_encrypt_carpass_passwords`: widens the column and encrypts what is
  still plaintext.
- **View.** `settings/dealer/_tabs/carpass.blade.php` renders an empty `x-ui.password` and says under
  it, in the `help` slot of `x-ui.field`, whether something is stored ("Er is een wachtwoord
  ingesteld. Laat leeg om het te behouden." / "Nog geen wachtwoord ingesteld.", in nl/en/fr/de/es).
  Whether something is stored is read from the raw column, not through the cast, so a row that has
  not been through the migration yet cannot make the tab throw.
- **Controller.** `DealerController::update` drops an empty `carpass_password` from the payload
  instead of writing it. The whole dealer sheet is one form, so without this every save of any other
  tab would wipe the credential. There is no reset button on this tab and none was invented; clearing
  a password is not something this screen offered before. `store()` is untouched: it writes
  `$request->validated()` and `carpass_password` is not a validated key, so a new dealer never got
  one there anyway.

## Migration safety

The cutover loads a fresh production dump on the same box with the SAME `APP_KEY`, and Forge runs
`migrate --force` after it, so this migration has to survive a table that is plaintext again and it
has to be safe to run twice.

- **Widen first, then encrypt.** `carpass_password` was `varchar(255)`. A six to twenty character
  password becomes a payload of roughly two hundred characters: it fits, but with nothing to spare,
  and a payload one character too long is silently truncated and the password is gone. The column is
  now `varchar(512)`, changed in the same migration, before a single row is written.
- **"Already encrypted?" is a real decrypt attempt**, `Crypt::decryptString()` in a try/catch, not a
  match on the `eyJpdiI6` prefix. The payload is base64 of a JSON object, so the prefix is a
  heuristic and a password that happened to start that way would be skipped forever. The prefix is
  used only as a fast path in the safe direction: something that does not start with it cannot be a
  payload, so there is nothing to try.
- **The write is a raw query builder update**, never the model, because the model now carries the
  cast and saving through it would encrypt the ciphertext a second time.
- **Chunked** (`chunkById`, 200 at a time), skipping `null` and `''`.
- The logic sits in `App\Support\CarpassPassword` rather than inside the migration closure, so it can
  be called twice in a test. A rule that cannot be run again cannot be proven to be idempotent.
- `down()` is deliberately empty: decrypting back to plaintext would undo the point, and narrowing
  the column again would truncate the payloads.

## Cutover note

`CUTOVER.md`, under step 2 (migrations after the fresh import): the encryption migration runs as part
of `migrate --force` and must run after the dump is loaded; from then on `APP_KEY` may not be replaced
without re-encrypting the column; and a production dump restored elsewhere no longer has working
Car-Pass credentials. That last one is the point, not a side effect.

## Checked

- `php artisan test --filter='Carpass|CarPass|Dealer|SmokeTest|StylesheetSyntaxTest|UiApiUsageTest|ClassReferencesResolveTest'`
  against a local MariaDB loaded from `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` with the post-dump
  migrations applied: 877 assertions, no failures. The route smoke test renders the dealer sheet, so
  the new tab markup is covered there too.
- `php artisan migrate --force` on that database: the migration runs and `show create table dealers`
  reports `carpass_password varchar(512)`.
- `APP_KEY=... php artisan view:cache` plus `php -l` on the compiled Car-Pass tab: no syntax errors.
- `php -l` on the five `dealer.php` language files.
- New tests in `tests/Feature/CarpassPasswordTest.php`: the tab contains neither the password nor its
  ciphertext; an empty submit keeps the stored value; a field that is not submitted at all keeps it;
  a typed value is stored encrypted (the raw column differs from what was typed, the model returns
  what was typed); the conversion over a mix of plaintext, ciphertext, empty and null rows converts
  only the plaintext one and converts nothing on a second run; and a value with the right prefix that
  is not a payload is not mistaken for one.

## Also worth a decision, not touched here

`settings.api_key` (the remove.bg key) is stored in plain text too:
`SettingsController::updateRemoveBg` writes `$request['api_key']` straight into the `settings` row,
`App\Http\Helpers\Photo` reads it raw, and `settings/setting/_tabs/removebg.blade.php` echoes it back
as the value of a plain text input. Same two problems, one shared key rather than one per dealer, and
a paid API. Left alone on purpose so it can be decided separately.
params.title: Car-Pass: the dealer password is encrypted at rest
